label: Brain
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human brain seen from the side
shortExplain: 🧠 The brain is the boss of the body! It sends messages to everything you do.
detailedExplain: 🧠 The brain controls the whole body through millions of messages that travel along nerves. It helps you think, dream, move, and feel emotions.

label: Heart
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human heart seen from the front
shortExplain: ❤️ Thump-thump, thump-thump! Your heart beats non-stop and pumps blood all over your body.
detailedExplain: ❤️ The heart is a muscle that pumps blood through tubes called blood vessels, carrying oxygen and energy to every part of your body.

label: Lungs
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the lungs and bronchi
shortExplain: 🫁 Your lungs fill up with air when you breathe, like two balloons.
detailedExplain: 🫁 The lungs bring oxygen from the air into your blood and release the carbon dioxide your body doesn't need, every time you breathe.

label: Stomach
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human stomach
shortExplain: 🫃 The stomach is like a bag that mixes food with special juices.
detailedExplain: 🫃 When you swallow food, it goes down to the stomach, where digestive juices turn it into a mush your body can use.

label: Liver
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the liver and where it sits in the body
shortExplain: 🟤 The liver cleans your blood and helps store energy for later.
detailedExplain: 🟤 The liver is like a little factory inside your belly: it cleans out things your body doesn't need, helps digest fats, and stores energy for when you need it.

label: Kidneys
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human kidneys
shortExplain: 🫘 Your kidneys filter your blood and make pee.
detailedExplain: 🫘 You have two kidneys, one on each side of your belly. They filter your blood like a strainer, taking out what your body doesn't need and turning it into pee.

label: Intestines
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the small intestine
shortExplain: 🌀 The intestines are long, coiled-up tubes that soak up nutrients from food.
detailedExplain: 🌀 After the stomach, food travels through the small intestine, where your body absorbs the nutrients, then through the large intestine before leaving as poop.

label: Bladder
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human bladder
shortExplain: 🎈 The bladder is like a little balloon that holds your pee until you go to the bathroom.
detailedExplain: 🎈 Your bladder fills up little by little with the pee your kidneys make. When it's full, you feel the urge to go to the bathroom and empty it.

label: Skin
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the layers of human skin
shortExplain: 🧴 Your skin covers your whole body and protects you, like a suit.
detailedExplain: 🧴 Skin is the body's biggest organ! It has several layers, protects you from germs and the sun, and lets you feel touch, heat, and cold.

label: Blood
shortExplain: 🩸 Blood travels all around your body, carrying food and air to your cells.
detailedExplain: 🩸 Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to every part of the body, and it also helps fight off germs that get in.

label: Skull
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human skull, front view
shortExplain: 💀 The skull is the hard bone that protects your brain, like a helmet.
detailedExplain: 💀 The skull is made of several bones fitted together that protect the brain from bumps. It also shapes your face!

label: Spine
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the spine, coloured by region
shortExplain: 🦴 The spine is the row of bones down your back that lets you bend.
detailedExplain: 🦴 The spine is made of many small bones called vertebrae, stacked on top of each other. It protects your spinal cord and lets you twist and bend your body.

label: Ribs
shortExplain: 🫁 Your ribs form a cage that protects your heart and lungs.
detailedExplain: 🫁 You have 12 pairs of ribs that curve around your chest like a strong cage, protecting your heart and lungs from bumps.

label: Femur
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the femur, the thigh bone
shortExplain: 🦵 The femur is the longest bone in your body — it's in your thigh!
detailedExplain: 🦵 The femur runs from your hip to your knee and is your strongest, longest bone. It carries your body's weight when you walk and jump.

label: Humerus
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the humerus, the upper-arm bone
shortExplain: 💪 The humerus is the long bone in your upper arm, between your shoulder and elbow.
detailedExplain: 💪 The humerus connects your shoulder to your elbow and is one of the bones you use most to throw a ball or give a hug!

label: Pelvis
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human pelvis
shortExplain: 🦴 The pelvis is the wide bone that connects your spine to your legs.
detailedExplain: 🦴 The pelvis forms a bony bowl that carries the weight of your body, protects important organs, and is where your legs attach.

label: Collarbone
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the human clavicle
shortExplain: 🦴 The collarbone is the thin bone you can feel at the base of your neck.
detailedExplain: 🦴 The collarbone (clavicle) connects your arm to the rest of your skeleton, and it's one of the bones that breaks most easily when you fall.

label: Kneecap
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the knee, showing the kneecap
shortExplain: 🦵 The kneecap (patella) is the round little bone at the front of your knee.
detailedExplain: 🦵 The kneecap protects the front of your knee and slides a little when you bend your leg, helping you walk, run, and squat.

label: Achilles Tendon
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the Achilles tendon, behind the ankle
shortExplain: 🦶 The Achilles tendon is the strong cord above your heel that lets you jump and run.
detailedExplain: 🦶 A tendon connects a muscle to a bone. The Achilles tendon connects your calf muscle to your heel bone, and it's the strongest tendon in the whole body!

label: Patellar Tendon
imageAlt: Medical illustration of the knee, showing the patellar tendon
shortExplain: 🦵 The patellar tendon connects your thigh muscle to your lower leg, just below the kneecap.
detailedExplain: 🦵 When you straighten your leg to kick a ball, it's the patellar tendon pulling the bone, connecting the strong thigh muscle to the lower part of your leg.

label: Ligaments
shortExplain: 🔗 Ligaments are strong ropes that connect bone to bone at your joints.
detailedExplain: 🔗 It's easy to mix up tendons and ligaments: a tendon connects muscle to bone, but a ligament connects bone to bone, holding joints like the knee or ankle firmly in place.

label: Cartilage
shortExplain: 👃 Cartilage is a bendy tissue, softer than bone — like the tip of your nose!
detailedExplain: 👃 Cartilage covers the ends of bones at joints to cushion them, and it also shapes your nose and ears, which is why they can bend without breaking.
